1. **Assess and prepare**: Inventory schema, extensions, roles, and total size (2 TB); select target managed service tier sized for current load plus headroom; confirm network path (VPN/peering), version compatibility, and required extensions are supported.
2. **Set up target environment**: Provision the managed PostgreSQL instance, replicate configuration (parameters, roles, extensions), and configure security groups, TLS, and IAM/DB credentials.
3. **Build replication/migration pipeline**: Configure logical replication (or a managed migration/CDC service) from on-prem to the target so initial bulk load and ongoing changes can stream with minimal lag.
4. **Full backup before any dry run touches production-derived data**: Take a full verified backup (base backup + WAL) of the production database and confirm it restores successfully before proceeding.
5. **Dry run / rehearsal on non-production data**: Using a restored copy or sanitized clone of production, execute the full migration procedure end-to-end (schema migration, bulk load, replication catch-up, cutover scripts, verification) against a staging target to validate timing, scripts, and rollback steps; record actual duration to confirm it fits the 2-hour window.
6. **Stakeholder communication (advance notice)**: At least one week and again 24 hours before the maintenance window, notify all ~4,000 users and internal stakeholders of the scheduled Sunday downtime, expected duration, and impact via email/status page/in-app banner.
7. **Pre-cutover full production backup**: Immediately before the maintenance window, take a fresh full backup (and confirm WAL archiving) of production as the guaranteed rollback point.
8. **Begin maintenance window — freeze writes**: Put the application into maintenance mode, stop write traffic to on-prem PostgreSQL, and let final replication/WAL catch up so source and target are in sync.
9. **Cutover**: Promote/finalize the target managed database, repoint application connection strings/DNS to the new endpoint, and restart application services pointing at the cloud database.
10. **Data integrity verification**: Compare row counts per table, checksums (e.g., pg_checksums or checksum queries per table), and sequence/index values between source and target; run smoke tests on critical application workflows before reopening traffic.
11. **Go-live or rollback decision**: If verification passes, remove maintenance mode and monitor closely; if verification fails or critical errors appear, execute rollback — repoint application back to the on-prem database (still intact and untouched since the freeze), restore from the pre-cutover backup if any corruption occurred, and communicate the delay/rollback to stakeholders.
12. **Post-migration monitoring and communication**: Monitor performance, replication lag (if keeping on-prem as standby for a few days), and error rates for 24–48 hours; send final confirmation to stakeholders and decommission the on-prem instance only after a defined retention/safety period.
